lines.japanese: 手紙はまだ続いていた。おじいさんは俺が≪コックピット≫を空にしている間、施設の職員たちに混じって何度か様子を見にきたらしい。
lines.english: The letter continued. While I had left the *Cockpit* vacant, the old man had apparently come with the facility staff several times to see how I was doing.

lines.japanese: おかげで、ここには俺が意識をなくしたときのことも書いてある。
lines.english: Thanks to that, he had written down what happened while I was unconscious too.

lines.japanese: 意識と体を切りはなした俺は呆けたようになり、より環境の整った大病院へ移送されることになった。
lines.english: After severing my consciousness from my body, I went blank, almost stupefied, and was transferred to a larger hospital with better facilities.

lines.japanese: 当日、小鳩はおじいさんに連れそわれて、担架で運ばれながら医療車両に乗せられる俺を見ていたらしい。
lines.english: On the day of the transfer, the old man accompanied Kobato as she watched me carried on a stretcher and loaded into a medical vehicle.

lines.japanese: 「やだぁ……」
「おにいちゃん、いっちゃやだよぅ」
lines.english: “Don’t go, Big Brother...”

lines.japanese: 小鳩が急に喋ったことで職員たちは驚いたらしい。兄の体に駆けよる彼女を止めることに気が回らなかった。
lines.english: The staff were apparently so startled when Kobato suddenly spoke that it did not occur to anyone to stop her as she ran to her brother's body.

lines.japanese: 「おにいちゃん、おにいちゃん！」
lines.english: “Big Brother! Big Brother!”

lines.japanese: そこからは俺も覚えている。その声が聞こえたんだ。
lines.english: From that point, I remember too. I heard her voice.

lines.japanese: だから俺は、小鳩のための完璧なお兄ちゃんになってやれないかなあと思った。
lines.english: And so I wondered whether I might become the perfect big brother for Kobato.

lines.japanese: 完璧なお兄ちゃん。あたかも聖騎士ホークのような、恐れを知らぬ無敵の勇者。それが俺の結論だった。
lines.english: The perfect big brother: a fearless, invincible hero, just like Holy Knight Hawk. That was my answer.

lines.japanese: 「おにいちゃん、おにいちゃああん！」
lines.english: “Big Brother! Big Brotherrr!”

lines.japanese: 「えっ……あれっ」
lines.english: “Huh...? What...?”

lines.japanese: 「小ばと？」
lines.english: “Ko... bato?”

lines.japanese: 「ふえっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、こばとのこと、わかる？」
lines.english: “Y-you know who Kobato is?”

lines.japanese: 「わかるよ、あたりまえじゃない」
lines.english: “Of course I do. How could I not?”

lines.japanese: 「ど、どうしたんだい急に？　君の名前は？」
lines.english: “Wh-what happened all of a sudden? What's your name?”

lines.japanese: 「ぼく……ぼくの名まえは……」
lines.english: “I... My name is...”

lines.japanese: チラと胸を見ると、そこにちょっと難しい漢字で名前が書いてあった。
lines.english: I flicked my eyes down at my chest. A name was written there in characters I found a little difficult to read.

lines.japanese: 「たかし……」
lines.english: “Takashi...”

lines.japanese: 「はねだたかし」
lines.english: “Takashi Haneda.”

lines.japanese: その後タカシとして順調に回復した俺は、小鳩と一緒に施設を出て、俺を引きとってくれることになった彼女の両親と暮らすことになった。
lines.english: After that, I recovered steadily as Takashi. Kobato and I left the institution together and went to live with her parents, who had agreed to take me in.

lines.japanese: 牧師のおじいさんは「何かあったら訪ねてきなさい」と小さな紙に連絡先を書いてよこした。
lines.english: The old pastor wrote his contact information on a little slip of paper and told us, “Come and see me if anything happens.”

lines.japanese: それから数週間。
lines.english: Several weeks passed.

lines.japanese: 小学校には戻ったものの、事件のことや、以前とまるで性格が違うことで、教室では常に一人だった。
lines.english: I returned to elementary school, but between the incident and my completely altered personality, I was always alone in the classroom.

lines.japanese: 給食の時間、教室で食べるといつも田畑の弟が牛乳をごはんにかけるから、俺はトイレにこもって一人で食べていた。
lines.english: At lunch, Tabata's little brother always poured milk over my rice if I ate in the classroom. So I locked myself in a bathroom stall and ate alone.

lines.japanese: 「あっ、だれかウンコしてんぞー！　だ～れだ、だれだ～、ウンコしてんの羽田！」
lines.english: “Hey! Somebody's taking a dump! Who is it? Who is it? Haneda's taking a dump!”

lines.japanese: クラスの男子がトイレに入ってきて、俺のこもる個室を何度も叩いた。中にいた俺は震えながら、残して先生に怒られないようにスプーンでけんちん汁を口に運んだ。
lines.english: The boys in my class crowded into the bathroom and pounded again and again on the stall where I hid. Trembling inside, I spooned root-vegetable soup into my mouth so I would not leave any and be scolded by the teacher.

lines.japanese: 「あー、そーいや今ど、父兄さんかんの日に、理科のけんきゅうはっぴょう会あるんだよなー。なあなあ、だれがやる？」
lines.english: “Oh, right. We’ve got science research presentations the next time parents come to watch class, don’t we? Hey, hey—who’s doing it?”

lines.japanese: 「河嶋、おまえやるぅ？」
lines.english: “Kawashima, you wanna?”

lines.japanese: 笑い声に混じって「えー、ヤダよ」という声が聞こえ、個室の外は盛りあがった。
lines.english: Through the laughter came a voice saying, “Ew, no way,” and the excitement outside my stall swelled.

lines.japanese: 「そーだ、こういうめんどくせーのは、羽田にやらしちゃえばいっか」
lines.english: “Oh, I know. We can make Haneda do this pain-in-the-ass crap.”

lines.japanese: さっきよりも大きな笑い声が聞こえて、賛成賛成とクラスメイトたちが手を叩いた。俺は大きな声を出すのが苦手で、当日のことを考えると少し気分が憂鬱になった。
lines.english: The laughter rose louder than before. My classmates clapped and chorused their approval. I was no good at projecting my voice, and the thought of presentation day left me mildly depressed.

lines.japanese: その時ふと気がついた。だったら大きな声を出すのが得意になればいいじゃん。
lines.english: Then it came to me. If that was the problem, why not become someone who was good at being loud?

lines.japanese: 「おーい、きこえてんのか便所メシ！　おまえ今日の学級会ではっぴょう会のせきにん決定だからな！」
lines.english: “Hey, can you hear me, Toilet-Lunch? At class meeting today, you're getting put in charge of the presentation!”

lines.japanese: 「すばらしい、感謝します田畑クン！　このおれを発表会の責任者に推せんしていただけるとは、なんたる光栄！　マーベラス！　さあ残り日数はわずかしかありません、アゲてアゲていきましょう！」
lines.english: “Splendid! My thanks, Tabata! What an honor, to be nominated leader of the presentation! Marvelous! Ladies and gentlemen, precious few days remain. Let's get fired up—and then fired up some more!”

lines.japanese: それからさらに数週間後。
lines.english: Several more weeks passed.

lines.japanese: 小学校の全校遠足。俺たちは山に行った。
lines.english: The whole elementary school went on a field trip to the mountains.

lines.japanese: 「おーい羽田あ！　おまえちょっと来いよ」
lines.english: “Hey, Haneda! Get over here a minute.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　うん、いま行くよ」
lines.english: “Huh? Okay, I'm coming.”

lines.japanese: 田畑の兄貴に呼ばれて行った場所は、切りくずしたようになっている崖だった。
lines.english: Tabata's older brother summoned me to a cliff face that looked as though a chunk had been gouged from it.

lines.japanese: その中ほどを指さして彼は言う。
lines.english: He pointed halfway up it.

lines.japanese: 「あそこにカブトムシいたっけ、羽田、おまえちょっと捕まえてこいよ」
lines.english: “There was a rhinoceros beetle up there, I think. Haneda, go catch it for me.”

lines.japanese: 田畑の兄貴は右手でぐいと虫取り網を突きつけてきた。
lines.english: Tabata's older brother shoved the insect net at me in his right hand.

lines.japanese: 「えっ、ムリだよ。あんなところまで僕は行けないよ」
lines.english: “What? I can't. I can't climb all the way up there.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえ！　俺が行けっつったら行くんだよ！　行けよハネダムシ！」
lines.english: “Shut up! When I tell you to go, you go! Move it, Haneda-bug!”

lines.japanese: 田畑の兄貴は俺を落とすくらいの勢いで、ぐいぐいと押してきた。
lines.english: Tabata's brother kept driving me forward, hard enough to send me over the edge.

lines.japanese: 「や、やめてよムリだよ、こんなところ……落ちちゃうよ……あっ」
lines.english: “S-stop it, I can't do this... I'll fall... Ah—”

lines.japanese: 「わあっ」
lines.english: “Whoa!”

lines.japanese: 前日に雨が降ったせいでぬかるんでいたのか、田畑の兄貴の方が滑ってしまった。
lines.english: The ground must have been muddy from the previous day's rain, because it was Tabata's brother who lost his footing.

lines.japanese: 「あっ、ああああっ」
lines.english: “Ah—aaaaah!”

lines.japanese: 斜面を滑りおちていく上級生。俺は手を伸ばそうとしたけど、腰が引けて動けなかった。
lines.english: The older boy went sliding down the slope. I tried to reach out, but my body recoiled in fear and I could not move.

lines.japanese: 「たっ、助けてえ！」
lines.english: “H-help me!”

lines.japanese: 大変だ、このままじゃ田畑の兄ちゃんが大ケガしてしまう。なのにどうしてか足は動いてくれなかった。
lines.english: This was terrible. At this rate, Tabata's brother would be badly hurt. Yet for some reason my feet refused to move.

lines.japanese: どうして僕には勇気がないんだろう。あそこにかわいそうなひとがいるんだ。誰か助けてあげて……そう思ったとき、鷹志の意識は急に薄れた。
lines.english: Why didn't I have any courage? There was someone in trouble right before me. Somebody, please save him... At that thought, Takashi's consciousness abruptly faded.

lines.japanese: 「だったら最初からタカシのことイジメんじゃねえよ」
lines.english: “Then maybe you shouldn't have picked on Takashi in the first place.”

lines.japanese: そして、田畑の兄ちゃんをつかむ俺の手があった。
lines.english: And then my hand was there, gripping Tabata's brother.

lines.japanese: 「は、羽田、おまえなんで……」
lines.english: “H-Haneda? Why did you...”

lines.japanese: 「ちげえよバカ、おまえなんか助けたんじゃねえよ。あれだあれ、カブトムシ捕まえんのに、おまえの持ってる虫取り網がほしかったんだよ」
lines.english: “Wrong, dumbass. I didn't save you. I wanted that, that thing—the bug net you've got. I need it to catch the beetle.”

lines.japanese: 田畑の兄ちゃんは、虫取り網なんかとっくに手から落として崖の下だった。
lines.english: Tabata's brother had dropped the bug net long ago. It lay at the bottom of the cliff.

lines.japanese: 俺たちは施設を出てからも、牧師のおじいさんの元へ行っては色んな話をした。
lines.english: Even after we left the institution, we often visited the old pastor and talked with him about all kinds of things.

lines.japanese: じいさんはタカシに強さを諭し、鷲介には人生の楽しみ方を話し、隼人には守る力を与えた。
lines.english: The old man taught Takashi strength, taught Shusuke how to enjoy life, and gave Hayato the power to protect.

lines.japanese: 「牧師さん……私にも、いい子にして待ってることを教えてくれた」
lines.english: “The pastor... taught me to be good and to wait, too.”

lines.japanese: そのじいさんが俺たちの前から居なくなった日。見送ったタカシの記憶が一つになったいま、最後の様子がようやく分かった。
lines.english: Then came the day the old man disappeared from our lives. Now that Takashi's memory of seeing him off had joined the rest, I finally knew what had happened in those last moments.

lines.japanese: 俺の記憶の中で、やつはやっぱり笑ってた。俺たちの肩に病人の手を置き、温かな目で笑う。
lines.english: In my memory, the old fellow was smiling after all. He laid the hands of a sick man on our shoulders and smiled with warmth in his eyes.

lines.japanese: 「今はばらばらの君たちが、一つになってよかったと思える日が必ず来る」
lines.english: “The day will surely come when all of you, separate now, will be glad to become one.”

lines.japanese: 「それまでは一人ずつが色々なことを見聞きし、悩み、楽しみながら歩きなさい。タカシ君、君もだ。それはすべて君の人生に役立つだろう」
lines.english: “Until then, each of you should make your own way, seeing and hearing all sorts of things, wrestling with worries and finding joy as you go. You too, Takashi. It will all serve you in the life ahead.”

lines.japanese: 「ひとは一人では生きられない。そう考えれば、つねに兄弟や妹と一緒にいるきみは心強いじゃないか」
lines.english: “No one can live alone. Look at it that way, and isn't it heartening that you are always together with your brothers and sister?”

lines.japanese: じいさんは肩を揺らして笑った。泣くことを知らなかった俺は、ひとりニコニコしていた。
lines.english: The old man laughed, his shoulders shaking. I did not know how to cry, so I alone stood there beaming.

lines.japanese: じいさんは居なくなり、叔父さんと叔母さんが中古とは言え柳木原に念願のマイホームを購入したので、俺たちも育った土地を離れることになった。
lines.english: After the old man was gone, my uncle and aunt finally bought the home they had always wanted in Yanagihara, secondhand though it was. And so we left the place where we had grown up.

lines.japanese: 一からの土地で、俺たちは新しい生き方を決めた。俺たちと小鳩。ふたり……いや、六人並んで羽田家の前に立つ。
lines.english: In a new place, starting from scratch, we chose a new way to live. Us, and Kobato. Two people... no, six of us, standing side by side before the Haneda home.

lines.japanese: そしていまも、こうしてふたりで立っている。
lines.english: And even now, here we stand, the two of us.

lines.japanese: 俺はすべてを思いだした。お母さんのことも事実を知った。
lines.english: I had remembered everything. I knew the truth about Mother too.

lines.japanese: だけど逃げずにここまで帰って来られた。
lines.english: And still I had made it all the way home without running.

lines.japanese: 小鳩やおじいさんがいなかったら、とても踏みとどまれなかっただろう。感謝しながら続きを読む。
lines.english: Without Kobato and the old man, I could never have held my ground. With gratitude, I read on.

lines.japanese: 「俺はいつか言ったな。俺たちの住む場所に都合のいい逃げ場なんてない。ここは天国じゃないんだ」
lines.english: “I told you once, didn’t I? There’s no easy escape in the world we live in. This isn’t heaven.”

lines.japanese: 「だがな、俺はおまえたちを見てると思うんだ。確かに俺たちは天使じゃないし、空を飛ぶことなんか出来ない」
lines.english: “But you know, when I look at all of you, I find myself thinking. It is true: we are not angels, and we cannot fly through the sky.”

lines.japanese: 「それでも羽ばたくことくらいは出来るんじゃないか。きっとおまえたち全員の力を合わせれば、この地上でも楽しく生きられるさ。なあ、おまえたち――」
lines.english: “Even so, maybe we can spread our wings. If all of you join forces, I know you can live happily even here on earth. Listen, you lot—”

lines.japanese: 俺は握っている手を見た。そこから目を上げていくと、やがてぶつかる穏やかな笑顔。
lines.english: I looked down at the hand in mine. My gaze traveled upward until, at last, it met a gentle smile.

lines.japanese: また明日から始まる平凡な日々を想像して、俺たちは微笑みあった。
lines.english: We imagined the ordinary days beginning again tomorrow, and smiled at each other.

lines.japanese: もうだいぶ古くなったノブを回して進む。
lines.english: I turned the knob, worn with the years, and stepped forward.

lines.japanese: 「ただいま、お兄ちゃん」
lines.english: “I’m home, Big Brother.”

lines.japanese: 「それと、おかえりなさい」
lines.english: “And welcome home.”

lines.japanese: 俺の日常。家族。大切なひと。これからはずっと一緒に生きていこう。
lines.english: My everyday life. My family. The people I loved. From now on, we would live on together, always.

lines.japanese: 俺はおじいさんの手紙をしまおうとして、もう一度だけ開いてみた。思わず笑いが漏れるおどけた結び文。
lines.english: I was about to put the old man's letter away when I opened it one last time. Its playful closing drew a laugh from me before I knew it.

lines.japanese: なあ、おまえたち――
lines.english: Listen, you lot—

lines.japanese: 「俺たちに翼はないこともないらしいぞ」
lines.english: “It seems we may not be entirely without wings after all.”
